about: BART (Bay Area Rapid Transit) website. The CLI lists stations and returns real-time departures, station timetables, service and elevator/escalator alerts, planned advisories, accessibility options, and routes, trips and fares from BART's public API.

commands.summary: Real-time departures (ETD) for a station: next trains per destination with minutes, platform, direction, length and line color (official BART API).

params.name: station
params.description: Uppercase 4-letter BART station code, e.g. EMBR, MONT, SFIA, 12TH

params.name: platform
params.description: Only departures from this platform number (1-4)

commands.summary: List all BART stations with name and station page URL. The slug in the URL (e.g. embr) is the station code.
Plan a BART trip between two stations: departure/arrival times, travel time, fare and legs (official BART API).

params.name: before
params.description: Number of trips before the given time (0-4)

params.name: after
params.description: Number of trips after the given time (1-4)

commands.summary: Fare between two BART stations (Clipper, cash and discount fares) from the official BART API.
List BART routes/lines with route number, name, abbreviation and color (official BART API).
Station details: name, address, description and lines serving the station.

params.name: station
params.description: Lowercase station slug from list-stations, e.g. embr, sfia, 12th

commands.summary: Full-day timetable of train departures from a station: line, train head station, departure time (official BART API).
Current BART service advisories (delays, disruptions) from the official BART API.
Planned service advisories (track work, bus bridges, line cancellations) from the RSS feed, with links to the full articles.
Elevator outage options and accessible paths for a station: what to do if you can't enter or exit.
Full text of a BART news article or planned service advisory, using the year and slug from its /news/articles/{year}/{slug} link.

params.name: year
params.description: Year segment of the article URL, e.g. 2026

params.name: slug
params.description: Article slug from the URL, e.g. news20261015
